facts.text: The Mayfield Memorial Library sits in one of Lawn’s historic Main Street buildings, preserving the town’s early 20th‑century charm.
When the railroad arrived in 1909, the original settlement became “Old Lawn,” and a new town incorporated in 1925 to serve rail workers.
Old Lawn vanished so completely that today there is no visible trace of its former streets or homes.
Lawn began as a modest water‑stop in the 1890s, located 24 miles south of Abilene along U.S. Highway 83.
During 1961, contractors flocked to Lawn to supply food and services for the construction of Dyess Atlas ICBM Site 6, just 2.4 miles east.
The town’s first settlement dates back to the 1890s, marking it as one of Taylor County’s earliest communities.
